I'll search for "solid oxide electrolyzer cell water vapor" first, as this seems most likely to involve high temperatures where water vapor would be used.

Based on the search results, I've found that Solid Oxide Electrolyzer Cells (SOECs) operate at high temperatures (700-900°C) and use water in the form of steam/vapor as the input. The other electrolyzer types (Alkaline, Anion exchange, and Proton exchange) typically use liquid water.

The key distinguishing feature of SOECs is that they operate at very high temperatures and use water in vapor form, while the other types operate at lower temperatures and use liquid water.
